title: Vanishing of Cech cohomology on a cofinal system of coverings implies vanishing of cohomology (any site)
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal B\subset\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ a set of objects, $\mathrm{Cov}$ a set of coverings of $\mathcal C$, and $\mathcal F\in\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$; $H^p(U,-)$ is cohomology over an object [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\check H^p$ Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. Assume: (1) for every $\mathcal U=\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ in $\mathrm{Cov}$ the objects $U$, $U_t$ and all $U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{t_p}$ lie in $\mathcal B$; (2) for every $U\in\mathcal B$ the coverings of $U$ occurring in $\mathrm{Cov}$ are cofinal among all coverings of $U$ (every covering of $U$ is refined by one in $\mathrm{Cov}$); (3) $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$ for all $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$ and $p>0$. Then $H^p(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for all $p>0$ and all $U\in\mathcal B$. (General-site version of [lem-weil-pbc-cech-vanishing-criterion], which is stated for the small etale site; same proof: embed $\mathcal F$ into an injective, Lemma 03AW, Lemma 03F8, dimension shifting.)
